newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Tech stocks busy, Chase spreads.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Tech stocks busy, Chase spreads.

text.p: Active options on technology stocks and a big spread in options on banking giant Chase Manhattan Corp were the features Tuesday, traders said.
Elsewhere, options on technology stocks once again drew heavy interest as the underlying stocks remained volatile, with many declining after recent rallies.
While the key Dow industrial average was up 16 points at 5,898, the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite index was off more than five points at 1,221.
"It seems like our option players are focussing on the stuff that really moves," said Rod Jamieson, vice president of option strategies at EVEREN Securities.
He added that there was large interest among retail investors in the technology sector.
"On days like this, when blue chips are acting better than Nasdaq, that doesn't really relate to our options market," he said, adding that options investors were playing both sides of the market.
"It was a combination. Guys buying calls, thinking that the techs are going to keep running, and guys buying puts, kind of playing a little downside move," he said.
Compaq Computer Corp had some of the busiest puts even though the stock was stuck in a tight range.
The Compaq October 65 put traded 6,950 contracts and the October 60 put trading 4,470. The most active Compaq call was the October 65, which traded just over 1,000 contracts.
Compaq shares were off 1/8 at 64 and traded between 63-5/8 and 64-7/8.
Jamieson said the Compaq options activity appeared to be investors taking bets on the stock rather than employing specific strategies.
Options on Micron Technology Inc, which was off 1-1/4 at 29-1/4, continued to be active, led by the October 30 call, which traded nearly 9,000 contracts.
The Micron October 35 call traded about 4,700. On the put side, October 25, 27-1/2 and 30 each traded 1,300 contracts.
Elsewhere, the Chase October 75 call traded 10,350 contracts by 1430 CDT (1930 GMT) and the November 75 call traded 9,150 contracts on the American Stock Exchange.
The October 75 call volume was all spreads, done in blocks of 9,000, 1,000, 200 and 150, while the November 75 volume was done in blocks of 9,000 and 150.

Traders said the action was most likely a calendar spread. The October 75 call traded at 5-3/4 and the November 75 call traded at 6-3/4. Few other Chase options were active, but the October 70 call traded more than 1,400 contracts.
One trader said it could have been a dividend-related calendar spread. The stock goes ex-dividend on Tuesday. --Gregory Crawford, 312-408-8750/E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com
